recipes.name: Anadama bread
recipes.englishName: New England molasses and cornmeal bread
recipes.description: A softly textured yeast loaf made with cornmeal and molasses, well suited to toast or a simple supper table.
ingredients: 430 g strong white bread flour, plus extra for kneading
instructions: Whisk warm water, yeast, cornmeal and molasses in a bowl. Leave 5 minutes, then stir in melted butter and salt.
Add flour gradually until a soft dough forms. Knead on a lightly floured surface for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled, about 60–90 minutes. Shape into a loaf and place in a greased 900 g tin.

Cover and rise until the dough crests just above the tin, about 35–50 minutes. Bake at 190°C conventional / 170°C fan for 35–40 minutes until deep brown and hollow-sounding underneath. Cool fully on a rack.
recipes.sides: Serve with butter, baked beans, chowder or sharp cheese.
recipes.substitutions: Use medium cornmeal if fine is unavailable; the crumb will be slightly coarser. Black treacle can replace molasses, though its flavour is stronger.
recipes.storage: Keep wrapped for 3 days at room temperature or freeze sliced for up to 2 months.
recipes.safety: Water should feel warm, not hot, before adding yeast. Cool bread completely before wrapping to avoid a damp crust.

recipes.name: Apple pie
recipes.description: A familiar baked pie of tart apples, cinnamon and a crisp pastry crust. Chill the pastry well for clean layers.
ingredients: 1.1 kg tart firm apples, peeled, cored and sliced
instructions: Rub butter into flour, 1 tbsp sugar and salt until pea-sized pieces remain. Add cold water a spoon at a time, bring together without kneading, divide into two discs and chill 30 minutes.
Toss apples with sugar, lemon, cinnamon and cornflour. Heat oven to 200°C conventional / 180°C fan and place a baking tray inside to heat.
Roll one pastry disc and line a 23 cm pie dish. Add apples in an even mound. Roll the second disc over the top, trim and crimp the edge; cut several steam vents.

Brush with egg wash. Set the dish on the hot tray and bake 20 minutes, then lower to 180°C / 160°C fan and bake 35–45 minutes until the crust is deeply golden and juices bubble through the vents. Rest at least 2 hours before slicing.
recipes.sides: Serve warm with vanilla ice cream, custard or cheddar.
recipes.substitutions: Use a mix of firm tart apples. A splash of water may replace lemon juice; omit cinnamon for a plainer filling.
recipes.storage: Cover and refrigerate after cooling; use within 4 days. Reheat slices in a low oven to crisp the pastry.
recipes.safety: The filling becomes very hot; allow the pie to rest before cutting. Keep raw egg wash and its brush away from ready-to-eat foods.

recipes.name: Boston baked beans
recipes.description: Navy beans bake slowly with molasses, mustard and pork until tender and richly flavoured. Begin with dried beans the night before.
ingredients: 1/2 tsp baking soda, for soaking water (optional)
150 g salt-cured pork belly or unsmoked bacon, diced
700 ml hot water, plus more as needed
instructions: Cover beans with plenty of cold water and add the optional baking soda if using. Soak 8–12 hours in the refrigerator. Drain, rinse, cover with fresh water and simmer 30–45 minutes until just beginning to soften; drain.
Heat oven to 150°C conventional / 130°C fan. Put pork and onion in a lidded ovenproof casserole. Add beans.
Whisk molasses, brown sugar, mustard, salt, pepper and hot water. Pour over beans; the liquid should nearly cover them. Cover tightly and bake 4 hours.
Check every hour; add boiling water if the beans are drying. Uncover for the final 30–45 minutes to thicken the sauce. Beans should be tender throughout; season after tasting.
recipes.sides: Serve with brown bread, franks, coleslaw or a simple green salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use smoked bacon for a smokier result. Maple syrup can replace some molasses but changes the characteristic flavour.
recipes.storage: Cool promptly, refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat until steaming hot; loosen with water if thick.
recipes.safety: Soak beans in the refrigerator and discard soaking water. Do not slow-cook dried kidney beans this way; this recipe uses navy beans, which are boiled before baking.

recipes.name: Banana pudding
recipes.description: Layers of vanilla custard, ripe bananas and crisp wafers soften into a chilled family-style dessert.
ingredients: 200 g vanilla wafers or plain tea biscuits
instructions: Warm milk in a saucepan until steaming but not boiling. Whisk egg yolks, sugar and cornflour in a bowl until smooth.
Slowly whisk the warm milk into the yolk mixture. Return to the pan and cook over medium-low heat, whisking continuously, until thick and bubbling for 1 minute.
Remove from the heat; whisk in vanilla and butter. Transfer to a shallow dish, press baking paper onto the surface and chill until cold.
In a serving dish layer wafers, banana slices and custard, repeating and finishing with custard. Chill at least 4 hours. Whip cream with icing sugar to soft peaks and spread on top before serving.
recipes.sides: Serve chilled on its own or with extra wafers.
recipes.substitutions: Use vanilla pudding mix prepared according to its label when short on time. Plain shortbread can replace vanilla wafers.
recipes.storage: Cover and refrigerate; best within 24 hours because bananas darken and wafers soften. Do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
recipes.safety: Cook the egg custard while whisking until it thickens and bubbles. Keep the finished dessert refrigerated.

recipes.name: Biscuits and sausage gravy
recipes.englishName: Buttermilk biscuits with peppered pork gravy
recipes.description: Flaky quick biscuits split under a creamy black-pepper gravy made in the same pan as browned breakfast sausage.
instructions: Heat oven to 220°C conventional / 200°C fan. Mix 300 g flour, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda and salt. Rub in butter until flaky crumbs form.
Stir in buttermilk just until a soft dough forms. Pat to 2 cm thick, fold once, pat again and cut 8 rounds. Bake on a lined tray for 12–15 minutes until risen and golden.
Meanwhile brown sausage in a skillet over medium heat, breaking into small pieces, until fully cooked with no pink remaining. Leave about 2 tbsp fat in the pan; drain excess if needed.
Sprinkle in 30 g flour and stir 1 minute. Gradually whisk in milk; simmer 5–8 minutes until thick. Add pepper, taste for salt and stir in chives. Split warm biscuits and spoon gravy over.
recipes.sides: Serve with eggs, fruit or sliced tomatoes for breakfast or brunch.
recipes.substitutions: Use unsalted butter and plain milk soured with 1 tbsp lemon juice in place of buttermilk. Turkey sausage works, though extra oil may be needed.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate gravy and biscuits separately for up to 3 days. Reheat gravy gently until steaming, adding milk to loosen; warm biscuits in the oven.
recipes.safety: Cook sausage thoroughly and avoid tasting raw dough. Refrigerate the milk-based gravy promptly.

recipes.name: Buffalo chicken wings
recipes.description: Crisp oven-baked wings tossed in a sharp cayenne and butter sauce, served with a cooling dip and crunchy vegetables.
ingredients: 1.2 kg chicken wings, split at joints and tips removed
1 tbsp baking powder (not bicarbonate of soda)
instructions: Pat wings very dry. Toss with baking powder, salt and pepper. Arrange on a rack over a foil-lined tray, leaving space between pieces; refrigerate uncovered 1 hour if time allows.
Heat oven to 220°C conventional / 200°C fan. Roast wings 45–50 minutes, turning halfway, until crisp and the thickest pieces reach 74°C internally.
Melt butter in a saucepan over low heat. Whisk in hot sauce and vinegar; keep warm without boiling.
Toss the hot wings with enough sauce to coat. Serve at once with celery, carrot and blue cheese dressing.
recipes.sides: Celery and carrot sticks with blue cheese dip are classic accompaniments.
recipes.substitutions: Use a milder pepper sauce and adjust the quantity to taste. A yoghurt-and-blue-cheese dip can replace bottled dressing.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat on a tray in a hot oven until crisp and steaming throughout.
recipes.safety: Use a clean thermometer in the thickest wing meat, avoiding bone; poultry must reach 74°C. Do not reuse sauce that touched raw chicken.

recipes.name: Chicken and dumplings
recipes.englishName: Chicken stew with soft drop dumplings
recipes.description: A one-pot chicken and vegetable stew finished with tender buttermilk dumplings steamed under a tight lid.
ingredients: 700 g boneless chicken thighs, in large pieces
instructions: Brown chicken in oil in a large lidded pot, in batches if necessary. Transfer to a plate. Soften onion, carrot and celery for 6 minutes.

Return chicken and juices; add stock and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook 25 minutes until chicken is tender and reaches 74°C in the thickest piece. Remove bay leaf and break chicken into large pieces.
Mix flour, baking powder and salt. Rub in butter, then stir in buttermilk just until a sticky dough forms. Stir peas into the stew.

Drop 8 spoonfuls of dough onto the gently simmering stew, spaced apart. Cover tightly and cook without lifting the lid for 15 minutes, until dumplings are puffed and cooked through. Scatter with parsley.
recipes.sides: Serve as a complete bowl meal; add green beans or a crisp salad if desired.
recipes.substitutions: Use cooked leftover chicken and reduce its simmer time; add it with the peas. Milk with 1 tsp lemon juice can stand in for buttermilk.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat gently until the stew and dumplings are steaming hot.
recipes.safety: Verify chicken reaches 74°C before shredding. Keep dumplings covered during cooking so their centres cook through.

recipes.name: Chicken-fried steak
recipes.englishName: Crisp beef steak with milk gravy
recipes.description: Tenderised beef is coated in seasoned crumbs, pan-fried until crisp and served with a simple peppered milk gravy.
ingredients: 4 tenderised beef cube steaks, about 150 g each
180 ml neutral oil, for shallow frying
instructions: Set up three shallow dishes: seasoned flour; eggs whisked with 120 ml milk; and breadcrumbs. Coat each steak in flour, dip in egg, then press into crumbs. Chill 10 minutes to help the coating adhere.

Heat 1 cm oil in a heavy skillet to about 175°C. Fry steaks in batches 3–4 minutes per side until deep golden and the centre reaches at least 63°C, then rest 3 minutes. Keep cooked steaks warm on a rack.
Pour off all but 2 tbsp frying oil. Whisk in 30 g flour and cook 1 minute. Slowly whisk in 450 ml milk and simmer until thick, scraping up browned bits.
Season gravy generously with black pepper and taste for salt. Spoon over steaks just before serving.
recipes.sides: Serve with mashed potatoes, green beans and the pepper gravy.
recipes.substitutions: Use thin boneless beef round steaks and tenderise evenly with a mallet. Buttermilk can replace the egg wash milk.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate steak and gravy separately for up to 3 days. Reheat steak on a rack in the oven; reheat gravy gently with a splash of milk.
recipes.safety: Keep raw beef and its coating dishes separate from cooked food. Fry in small batches; carefully monitor hot oil and verify steak temperature with a thermometer.

recipes.name: Chicken pot pie
recipes.englishName: Chicken and vegetable pie with a flaky lid
recipes.description: Chicken, vegetables and a lightly seasoned creamy sauce bake beneath a golden pastry lid for a practical family supper.
ingredients: 500 g cooked chicken, cut into bite-size pieces
1 sheet ready-rolled puff pastry, about 320 g
instructions: Heat oven to 200°C conventional / 180°C fan. Soften onion and carrots in 1 tbsp butter for 6–8 minutes; stir in peas and cooked chicken.
In a saucepan melt 40 g butter, stir in flour and cook 1 minute. Whisk in stock gradually, then milk and thyme. Simmer 3–4 minutes until smooth and lightly thickened.
Combine sauce and chicken mixture in a 1.5 litre baking dish. Let filling cool 10 minutes so the pastry stays crisp.
Lay pastry over the dish, trim and press edges to seal. Cut a small steam vent and brush with egg. Bake 30–35 minutes until puffed, deeply golden and bubbling. Rest 10 minutes before serving.
recipes.sides: Serve with steamed greens or a simple salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use leftover turkey or cooked mushrooms and white beans. Shortcrust pastry can replace puff pastry; follow its pack temperature guidance.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat portions until piping hot in the centre.
recipes.safety: Use only fully cooked chicken in the filling and heat the pie until bubbling throughout. Keep raw egg wash away from the cooked pie.

recipes.name: Chili con carne, Texas-style
recipes.description: A thick beef stew built around dried chiles, cumin and stock. This version leaves out beans so the beef and chile sauce stay central.
ingredients: 1.2 kg beef chuck, trimmed and cut into 2 cm cubes
3 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
instructions: Toast dried chiles in a dry pan for 20–30 seconds per side until fragrant, not scorched. Cover with hot water for 20 minutes; drain and blend with 150 ml fresh water until smooth.
Pat beef dry. Brown in oil in batches in a heavy pot; transfer to a plate. Soften onion 6 minutes, then add garlic, cumin, oregano and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Return beef and juices. Stir in chile puree and stock; bring just to a simmer. Cover and cook on low heat 2–2 1/2 hours, stirring occasionally, until beef is fork-tender.
Uncover for the final 15 minutes to thicken. Stir in vinegar, season to taste and rest 10 minutes before serving.
recipes.sides: Serve with warm tortillas, cornbread, chopped onion and grated cheese.
recipes.substitutions: Use a mild dried chile blend; add a little smoked paprika if ancho chiles are unavailable. Add beans only as a personal variation, not as part of this Texas-style version.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate promptly and use within 3 days; the flavour deepens overnight. Reheat until bubbling throughout.
recipes.safety: Wear gloves when handling chiles and avoid touching eyes. Keep raw beef separate and simmer until tender; chill leftovers promptly.

recipes.name: Clam chowder, New England-style
recipes.description: A creamy, pale chowder of clams, potatoes, onion and bacon, served with crackers or bread. Keep the simmer gentle after adding dairy.
ingredients: 400 g potatoes, peeled and cut into 1.5 cm cubes
250 ml bottled clam juice or strained clam liquor
instructions: Cook bacon in a heavy saucepan until it releases fat and begins to crisp. Add butter, onion and celery; cook gently for 6 minutes without browning.
Add potatoes, clam juice, water, bay leaf and thyme. Simmer 12–15 minutes until potatoes are just tender; remove bay leaf.
Stir in milk and cream and warm gently until steaming, not boiling. Add cooked clams and heat 2–3 minutes until hot.
Season with pepper and parsley. If thicker chowder is desired, mash a few potato pieces into the broth. Serve hot.
recipes.sides: Oyster crackers or toasted bread are traditional-style accompaniments.
recipes.substitutions: Use canned chopped clams and their strained liquid. Half-and-half can replace milk and cream together; do not boil after adding dairy.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate promptly and use within 2 days. Reheat gently until steaming; avoid repeated reheating.
recipes.safety: Use clams from a reputable source and keep chilled. Cooked clams should be heated until steaming; discard any shellfish with an off smell.

recipes.name: Cobb salad
recipes.englishName: Chopped chicken, egg and avocado salad
recipes.description: A composed salad of crisp greens, chicken, egg, avocado, tomato, bacon and blue cheese with a tangy vinaigrette.
ingredients: 300 g cooked chicken breast, cooled and diced
instructions: Whisk olive oil, vinegar, mustard, salt and pepper in a small bowl.
Arrange chopped lettuce over a large platter. Place chicken, eggs, avocado, tomato, bacon and blue cheese in separate rows over the greens.
Drizzle dressing over just before serving, or pass it at the table. Toss gently if a mixed salad is preferred.
recipes.sides: Serve with crusty bread or soup for a fuller meal.
recipes.substitutions: Use turkey or leftover roast chicken. Feta may replace blue cheese; omit bacon for a meat-free variation.
recipes.storage: Keep components and dressing separately refrigerated for up to 2 days; cut avocado shortly before serving. Do not store dressed leftovers for long.
recipes.safety: Keep cooked chicken and eggs chilled until serving and discard food left at room temperature for more than 2 hours.

recipes.name: Cornbread skillet
recipes.description: A quick cornmeal bread baked in a hot skillet, with crisp edges and a tender centre. This version is lightly sweetened.
ingredients: 60 g butter, melted, plus 1 tbsp for skillet
instructions: Heat oven to 220°C conventional / 200°C fan. Put a 23 cm cast-iron skillet in the oven with 1 tbsp butter to heat.
Whisk cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder and salt. In another bowl whisk egg, buttermilk and melted butter.
Fold wet ingredients into dry just until combined; a few small lumps are fine. Carefully remove hot skillet and swirl to coat with butter.
Pour batter into the skillet and bake 20–25 minutes until golden and a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean. Rest 10 minutes before cutting.
recipes.sides: Serve warm with beans, greens, chilli or butter and honey.
recipes.substitutions: If buttermilk is unavailable, stir 1 tbsp lemon juice into 300 ml milk and stand 5 minutes. Reduce sugar for a savoury version.
recipes.storage: Keep covered for 2 days at room temperature or refrigerate for up to 4 days. Reheat wedges briefly in the oven.
recipes.safety: Use oven gloves when handling the hot skillet. Avoid overmixing, which can make the crumb tough.

recipes.name: Cranberry sauce
recipes.region: New England and nationwide holiday tables
recipes.description: Whole cranberries simmer with orange and sugar until they pop and form a tart, spoonable sauce.
ingredients: 1 small orange, finely zested and juiced
instructions: Rinse fresh cranberries and remove any shrivelled berries. Put cranberries, sugar, water, orange zest, orange juice and salt in a saucepan.
Bring to a gentle boil over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves. Lower heat and simmer 10–12 minutes; berries will pop and the liquid will thicken.
Remove from heat while the sauce is slightly looser than desired; it thickens as it cools. Chill before serving.
recipes.sides: Serve with roast turkey, chicken, sandwiches or sharp cheese.
recipes.substitutions: Use lemon zest instead of orange or replace up to half the water with apple juice. Adjust sugar after tasting once cool.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate in a covered container for up to 7 days or freeze for 2 months.
recipes.safety: Use a saucepan large enough to prevent bubbling sauce from splashing. Cool promptly before refrigeration.

recipes.name: Detroit-style pizza
recipes.englishName: Pan pizza with crisp cheese edges
recipes.description: A thick, airy pan pizza with cheese spread to the edges for a caramelised crust and stripes of tomato sauce on top.
ingredients: 1 tbsp olive oil, plus extra for pan
instructions: Mix flour, yeast and salt. Add warm water and olive oil; stir to a sticky dough. Cover and rise until doubled, about 60–90 minutes.
Oil a 23 x 33 cm deep metal pan generously. Transfer dough and gently stretch toward corners. Rest 15 minutes, then stretch again. Heat oven to 240°C conventional / 220°C fan.
Scatter cheese evenly to the pan edges, add pepperoni if using, and spoon sauce in three lengthwise stripes over the top. Sprinkle with oregano.
Bake on the lower rack 15–18 minutes until the edges are dark golden and crisp and the centre is cooked. Loosen edges with a thin spatula, lift out, rest 5 minutes and cut.
recipes.sides: Serve with a green salad and extra tomato sauce at the table.
recipes.substitutions: Use all mozzarella or a blend with Monterey Jack. A 25 cm square metal pan works; adjust baking time if the dough is thinner.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours for up to 3 days. Reheat slices in a covered skillet to crisp the base.
recipes.safety: Use oven gloves and take care of hot cheese and oil. The centre should be fully baked before slicing.

recipes.name: Fried green tomatoes
recipes.description: Firm unripe tomatoes are coated in seasoned cornmeal and pan-fried until crisp outside and tender inside.
ingredients: 4 firm green tomatoes, sliced 1 cm thick
150 ml neutral oil, for shallow frying
instructions: Lay tomato slices on a rack, sprinkle lightly with salt and leave 10 minutes. Blot moisture with kitchen paper.
Place flour in one dish. Whisk eggs and buttermilk in a second. Mix cornmeal, breadcrumbs, pepper and paprika in a third.
Dip each slice in flour, then egg mixture, then cornmeal mixture, pressing coating on. Rest coated slices 5 minutes.
Heat a shallow layer of oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry in batches 2–3 minutes per side until golden and tender. Drain on a rack and serve hot.
recipes.sides: Serve as a side, in a sandwich or with a tangy yoghurt dip.
recipes.substitutions: Use fine polenta in place of cornmeal; avoid ripe soft tomatoes, which release too much moisture.
recipes.storage: Best eaten immediately. Refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days and re-crisp in a hot oven.
recipes.safety: Maintain moderate oil heat to prevent splattering. Keep wet coating ingredients away from ready-to-eat foods.

recipes.name: Fried chicken, Southern-style
recipes.description: Chicken pieces soak in seasoned buttermilk, then fry in a craggy flour coating until crisp and cooked through.
instructions: Mix buttermilk, salt, paprika, garlic powder and pepper. Add chicken, cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight.
Combine flour, baking powder and cayenne. Lift chicken from buttermilk, let excess drip off, then coat firmly in flour. Rest on a rack 15 minutes.
Heat 4–5 cm oil in a heavy pot to 170°C. Fry a few pieces at a time, turning occasionally, 12–18 minutes depending on size; keep oil near 160–170°C.
Transfer to a rack and check the thickest part of every piece reaches 74°C without touching bone. Rest 5 minutes before serving.
recipes.sides: Serve with coleslaw, biscuits, greens or mashed potatoes.
recipes.substitutions: Use plain yoghurt thinned with milk instead of buttermilk. Boneless thighs cook faster; verify temperature rather than relying on time.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat on a rack in a 190°C oven until steaming hot and crisp.
recipes.safety: Deep frying can cause severe burns. Use a deep heavy pot, never fill it more than halfway, dry the outside of the chicken, and never add water to hot oil. Poultry must reach 74°C.

recipes.name: Grits with cheddar
recipes.description: Coarsely ground corn cooks slowly with water and milk into a smooth savoury porridge finished with butter and cheddar.
ingredients: 180 g stone-ground white or yellow grits
instructions: Bring water, milk and salt to a gentle boil in a heavy saucepan. Slowly whisk in grits to prevent lumps.
Lower heat to the lowest steady simmer. Cook uncovered 25–35 minutes, stirring frequently and scraping the bottom, until soft and creamy. Add a little hot water if too thick.
Remove from heat and stir in butter and cheddar until melted. Season with pepper and taste for salt. Serve immediately.
recipes.sides: Serve with eggs, greens, beans, grilled vegetables or shrimp.
recipes.substitutions: Quick grits cook faster; follow their package ratio and time. Use stock instead of some water for a savoury base.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours for up to 3 days. Reheat slowly with milk or water, stirring until steaming.
recipes.safety: Stir carefully as thick porridge can bubble and splatter. Use the package directions for instant or quick-cooking varieties.

recipes.name: Hoppin' John
recipes.description: Black-eyed peas simmer with rice, onion and smoked pork for a hearty one-pot dish of the South Carolina Lowcountry.
ingredients: 300 g dried black-eyed peas, picked over
150 g smoked ham hock or diced smoked ham
instructions: Cover dried peas with cold water and soak 6–8 hours, preferably refrigerated. Drain and rinse.
Warm oil in a pot. Soften onion, celery and green pepper for 6 minutes; add garlic and thyme for 30 seconds.
Add peas, ham, bay leaf and water. Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer partly covered 40–55 minutes until peas are nearly tender. Remove ham hock, shred meat and return it to the pot.
Stir in rice and enough liquid to cover by about 2 cm. Cover tightly and cook on low 18–20 minutes until rice is tender and liquid absorbed. Rest 10 minutes, fluff and top with spring onion.
recipes.sides: Serve with collard greens, cornbread, hot sauce or sliced tomatoes.
recipes.substitutions: Use canned black-eyed peas: add them with the rice and reduce the liquid, checking the rice package ratio. Omit smoked pork and use vegetable stock for a meat-free pot.
recipes.storage: Cool promptly, refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat until steaming throughout, adding a little water if dry.
recipes.safety: Soak dried peas in the refrigerator and cook until completely tender. Refrigerate cooked rice promptly and reheat only once until steaming hot.

recipes.name: Jambalaya
recipes.description: Rice cooks in one pot with browned sausage, chicken, vegetables and seasoned stock. This Creole-leaning home version uses tomatoes.
instructions: Brown sausage in a heavy lidded pot; transfer to a plate. Add oil and brown chicken until golden on the outside; transfer beside sausage.
Cook onion, pepper and celery for 6–8 minutes. Add garlic, paprika and thyme; stir 30 seconds.

Stir in rinsed rice, tomatoes, stock and bay leaf. Return sausage and chicken with their juices. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer on low 22–25 minutes without stirring, until rice is tender and chicken reaches 74°C. If rice is not yet tender and the pan is dry, add a little hot stock and continue cooking.
Turn off heat and rest covered 10 minutes. Remove bay leaf, fluff gently and top with spring onion.
recipes.sides: Serve with hot sauce, green salad or cornbread.
recipes.substitutions: Use smoked kielbasa if andouille is unavailable; season to taste because salt levels vary. Add peeled prawns during the final 5–6 minutes if desired.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat rice dishes until steaming hot throughout; reheat once only.
recipes.safety: Verify chicken reaches 74°C and refrigerate cooked rice promptly. Keep raw poultry separate from vegetables and cooked sausage.

recipes.name: Key lime pie
recipes.description: A tangy baked lime filling sits in a crumb crust and chills until sliceable. Ordinary limes work when Key limes are unavailable.
ingredients: 220 g digestive or graham-style biscuits, finely crushed
1 x 397 g tin sweetened condensed milk
120 ml Key lime juice or fresh lime juice
instructions: Heat oven to 180°C conventional / 160°C fan. Mix biscuit crumbs, melted butter and sugar. Press firmly into a 23 cm pie plate and bake 10 minutes; cool slightly.
Whisk egg yolks 2 minutes until thickened. Whisk in condensed milk, lime juice and zest until smooth.
Pour filling into the crust and bake 15 minutes until the edges are set and the centre still has a slight wobble. Cool, then refrigerate at least 4 hours.
Whip cream with icing sugar to soft peaks. Spread or pipe on the chilled pie and add a little zest before slicing.
recipes.sides: Serve well chilled with softly whipped cream.
recipes.substitutions: Use ordinary Persian limes if Key limes are unavailable. Plain graham crackers or digestive biscuits both work for the crust.
recipes.storage: Cover and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Do not leave the pie out for more than 2 hours.
recipes.safety: The filling contains egg and dairy; keep refrigerated. Use pasteurised eggs if serving to someone at higher risk from foodborne illness.

recipes.name: Lobster rolls, Maine-style
recipes.englishName: Chilled lobster salad in toasted rolls
recipes.description: Sweet cooked lobster is lightly dressed with mayonnaise, lemon and celery, then tucked into butter-toasted split-top rolls.
ingredients: 450 g cooked lobster meat, chilled and cut into bite-size pieces
instructions: Check cooked lobster meat for shell fragments and keep chilled. Gently combine with mayonnaise, lemon, celery and chives; season lightly with salt and pepper.
Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat. Toast the sides of each roll until golden, about 1–2 minutes per side.
Divide chilled lobster salad among the warm rolls and serve promptly.
recipes.sides: Serve with potato chips, a pickle and coleslaw.
recipes.substitutions: Use cooked crab or prawns for a different seafood roll. Keep mayonnaise minimal so the lobster remains the focus.
recipes.storage: Keep lobster salad refrigerated and use within 1 day. Toast rolls just before serving; do not leave filled rolls at room temperature.
recipes.safety: Buy lobster from a reputable source, keep it cold and discard seafood left out for more than 2 hours. This recipe uses cooked lobster, not raw seafood.

recipes.name: Macaroni and cheese
recipes.description: Elbow macaroni is folded through a smooth cheddar sauce and baked under a light crumb topping until bubbling.
instructions: Heat oven to 190°C conventional / 170°C fan. Cook macaroni in salted boiling water until 2 minutes short of package time. Drain.
Melt butter in a saucepan. Stir in flour and cook 1 minute. Gradually whisk in warm milk; simmer 4–5 minutes, whisking, until smooth and thick enough to coat a spoon.
Stir in mustard, salt, pepper and most of the cheddar until melted. Fold in macaroni and transfer to a baking dish.
Mix breadcrumbs with oil and remaining cheese; scatter over. Bake 20–25 minutes until bubbling and lightly browned. Rest 5 minutes.
recipes.sides: Serve with green salad, roasted vegetables or stewed tomatoes.
recipes.substitutions: Use a mix of cheddar and Monterey Jack. Add peas or cooked broccoli for a vegetable variation.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat covered until piping hot; add a splash of milk if dry.
recipes.safety: Cool leftovers promptly and reheat only once. Stir the sauce over moderate heat to prevent scorching.

recipes.name: Meatloaf
recipes.description: A seasoned loaf of beef and pork is baked with a simple tomato glaze; breadcrumbs and milk keep the slices tender.
instructions: Heat oven to 180°C conventional / 160°C fan. Mix breadcrumbs and milk; leave 5 minutes to soften.
Add beef, pork, egg, onion, Worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper. Mix gently with clean hands just until combined; do not compress heavily.
Shape into a loaf in a shallow roasting tin. Mix ketchup, brown sugar and vinegar; brush half over the top.
Bake 40 minutes. Brush with remaining glaze and bake 20–25 minutes more until the centre reaches 71°C. Rest 10 minutes before slicing.
recipes.sides: Serve with mashed potatoes, peas, green beans or a simple salad.
recipes.substitutions: Use all beef or replace pork with minced turkey; leaner mixtures may be drier. Oats can replace breadcrumbs by equal weight.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat slices until steaming hot or freeze portions for up to 2 months.
recipes.safety: Because it contains minced meat, check the centre reaches 71°C. Wash hands and surfaces after handling raw meat.

recipes.name: Peach cobbler
recipes.englishName: Baked peaches with a biscuit topping
recipes.description: Juicy peaches bake under a tender spooned biscuit topping until the fruit bubbles and the top turns golden.
ingredients: 900 g ripe peaches, peeled if desired and sliced
instructions: Heat oven to 190°C conventional / 170°C fan. Toss peaches with 100 g sugar, lemon juice, cornflour and cinnamon in a baking dish.
Mix flour, 2 tbsp sugar, baking powder and salt. Rub in butter until coarse crumbs form. Stir in milk just until a soft dough forms.
Drop spoonfuls of dough over the peaches, leaving small gaps for steam. Sprinkle with coarse sugar.
Bake 35–40 minutes until topping is golden and fruit juices bubble at the edges. Rest 15 minutes before serving.
recipes.sides: Serve warm with vanilla ice cream or custard.
recipes.substitutions: Use drained canned peaches or thawed frozen peaches; reduce added sugar if packed in syrup. A little nutmeg can replace cinnamon.
recipes.storage: Cover and refrigerate within 2 hours; use within 3 days. Reheat in the oven to refresh the topping.
recipes.safety: The fruit filling stays very hot after baking. Let it rest before serving, especially to children.

recipes.name: Pecan pie
recipes.description: Toasted pecans sit in a sweet brown-sugar filling in a single pastry shell; bake until the centre is just set.
ingredients: 1 x 23 cm unbaked shortcrust pie shell
120 ml golden syrup or corn syrup
instructions: Heat oven to 180°C conventional / 160°C fan. Spread pecans on a tray and toast 6–8 minutes, then cool. Place pie shell on a baking tray.
Whisk eggs, brown sugar, syrup, melted butter, vanilla and salt until smooth. Arrange pecans in the shell and pour filling over.
Bake 45–55 minutes until the edges are set and the centre jiggles slightly but is not liquid. Cover crust edges with foil if they brown too quickly.
Cool completely, at least 3 hours, to allow the filling to set before slicing.
recipes.sides: Serve at room temperature with lightly whipped cream.
recipes.substitutions: Maple syrup can replace golden syrup for a different flavour. Use a ready-made pastry shell or a home-baked shortcrust base.
recipes.storage: Cover and refrigerate within 2 hours; use within 4 days. Bring slices briefly toward room temperature before serving.
recipes.safety: The filling contains eggs and nuts. Check for allergies and keep the cooled pie refrigerated.

recipes.name: Pork tenderloin sandwich
recipes.description: A thin, broad breaded pork cutlet is fried crisp and served in a bun with simple toppings.
ingredients: 500 g pork tenderloin, cut into 4 medallions
150 ml neutral oil, for shallow frying
Lettuce, tomato, onion and mustard to serve
instructions: Place each pork medallion between baking paper and pound evenly to about 8 mm thick, wider than the buns. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Set out flour, eggs whisked with milk, and breadcrumbs. Coat each cutlet in flour, egg, then breadcrumbs; press coating on and rest 10 minutes.
Heat 1 cm oil in a skillet to about 170°C. Fry cutlets one or two at a time for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and the centre reaches 63°C; rest at least 3 minutes.
Drain briefly on a rack. Serve in buns with lettuce, tomato, onion and mustard.
recipes.sides: Serve with pickles, potato salad or oven fries.
recipes.substitutions: Use thin pork loin chops if tenderloin is unavailable. Panko gives a lighter, coarser crust than fine crumbs.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate cooked cutlets within 2 hours for up to 3 days. Reheat on a rack in a hot oven until crisp and steaming.
recipes.safety: Keep raw pork separate from toppings and cooked food. Check the centre reaches 63°C and rest for 3 minutes; follow local food-safety guidance.

recipes.name: Pot roast
recipes.region: New England and nationwide home cooking
recipes.description: A well-browned beef chuck roast braises slowly with onions, carrots and potatoes until fork-tender, making its own savoury gravy.
instructions: Pat roast dry and season with salt and pepper. Heat oven to 160°C conventional / 140°C fan. Brown roast in oil in a heavy ovenproof pot on all sides; transfer to a plate.
Brown onions, carrots and celery for 5 minutes. Stir in flour and tomato paste for 1 minute, then slowly add stock, scraping browned bits from the base.
Return roast and juices. Add bay leaves and thyme; liquid should come about one-third up the meat. Cover tightly and braise in the oven for 2 1/2 hours.
Add potatoes, cover and cook 45–60 minutes more until vegetables are tender and beef pulls apart easily. Remove bay leaves, skim fat and rest roast 10 minutes before slicing or shredding.
recipes.sides: Serve with the braised vegetables, pan gravy and crusty bread.
recipes.substitutions: Use a boneless brisket or blade roast of similar size and adjust time until fork-tender. Add parsnips with the potatoes.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate meat and gravy within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat gently until steaming throughout.
recipes.safety: Keep raw beef separate from vegetables and cooked foods. Braise until fork-tender; refrigerate leftovers promptly in shallow containers.

recipes.name: Shrimp and grits
recipes.englishName: Garlic shrimp over creamy corn grits
recipes.description: Quickly sautéed shrimp with garlic and lemon are spooned over creamy grits for a coastal Southern meal.
ingredients: 500 g raw peeled shrimp, thawed if frozen
instructions: Bring water, milk and salt to a gentle boil. Whisk in grits slowly, lower heat and cook 25–35 minutes, stirring often, until soft. Stir in butter and cheddar.
Pat shrimp dry and season with paprika and black pepper. Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook shrimp in a single layer 1–2 minutes per side, turning once, until opaque and the thickest part reaches 63°C. Add garlic for the final 30 seconds; stir in lemon juice and parsley.
Spoon grits into warm bowls and top with shrimp and pan juices. Serve immediately.
recipes.sides: Serve with sliced tomatoes, greens or cornbread.
recipes.substitutions: Use quick grits according to package directions. Add a little stock to the grits instead of some milk for a less rich bowl.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate shrimp and grits separately within 2 hours and use within 2 days. Reheat gently until steaming; loosen grits with milk or water.
recipes.safety: Thaw shrimp in the refrigerator, not on the counter. Cook until opaque and 63°C; keep raw seafood separate from cooked food.

recipes.name: Sweet potato casserole
recipes.englishName: Mashed sweet potatoes with pecan topping
recipes.description: Mashed baked sweet potatoes are seasoned lightly and topped with pecans and oats for a crisp holiday side.
instructions: Heat oven to 200°C conventional / 180°C fan. Pierce sweet potatoes and bake on a tray 40–50 minutes until very soft. Cool enough to handle, then scoop flesh into a bowl.
Mash with melted butter, milk, egg, 2 tbsp brown sugar, cinnamon and salt. Spread in a greased 1.5 litre baking dish.
Mix pecans, oats, flour, cold butter and 1 tbsp brown sugar with fingertips until crumbly. Scatter evenly over the potatoes.
Bake at 180°C / 160°C fan for 20–25 minutes until set and the topping is golden. Rest 10 minutes before serving.
recipes.sides: Serve beside roast turkey, ham, beans or greens.
recipes.substitutions: Use walnuts instead of pecans or omit nuts and add extra oats. Reduce sugar for a savoury side.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Reheat covered until steaming hot; crisp the topping uncovered for the final few minutes.
recipes.safety: The casserole contains egg and nuts. Check allergy needs and cook until the centre is set and steaming.
